title: Health stocks up, tech stocks down on Friday
summary: On the last trading day of the week, healthcare companies on the Nasdaq rose about 2.1% on average, while technology companies slipped about 0.6%.
why: When money moves from one group of stocks to another, people call it a rotation. One day is not a trend, but if it keeps happening, our tech-heavy companies could lag while health companies like Eli Lilly do better.

title: TSMC's sales jumped 55% in a year
summary: TSMC, the factory that builds chips for NVIDIA, AMD and Apple, reported September sales of about NT$512 billion, 54.6% more than a year earlier. Sales for the first nine months of 2026 grew about 41%.
why: TSMC builds the chips that power AI. When its sales keep growing this fast, it means companies are still buying lots of AI chips, which is good news for the AI suppliers on our list.

title: The Fed may raise interest rates again
summary: Notes from the Federal Reserve's last meeting showed most officials expect another rate increase this year, because prices are still rising about 3.4% a year, well above their 2% goal. The Fed already raised rates in September.
why: Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive and make safe savings pay more. That can pull money away from stocks, especially fast-growing companies that look expensive, like many AI stocks.

title: Coming up: the Fed decides on rates Oct. 28-29
summary: The Federal Reserve's next meeting is October 28-29. According to the same report, traders expect the Fed to wait at that meeting and raise rates in December.
why: Fed meeting days often make the whole market jumpy. A surprise in either direction can move every stock on our list.

title: Rocket Lab's big new rocket might slip to 2027
summary: Rocket Lab said the window to launch its larger Neutron rocket before the end of 2026 is narrowing, and a filing said the first flight could slip into 2027. A fuel tank broke during a test in January, which already caused a delay.
why: Investors are paying today for rockets Rocket Lab plans to fly tomorrow. Delays push back the money those launches would earn, which is one reason the stock is far below its high.
